speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how effective have the previous downturn measures been in helping workers to stay in their jobs or find new opportunities; and (b) what are the plans that the Ministry has in place to support workers should the economy continue to slow down and jobs may be lost.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our current situation and outlook are different from that in 2008.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, in the first half of 2009, retrenchments exceeded 19,000 when, in a typical year during that period, retrenchments would be about 15,000.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But in the first half of 2009 alone, retrenchments were 19,000.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Job losses estimated for the whole year, some analysts came in with numbers, such as 100,000.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That was the situation in the beginning of 2009.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If we look at the situation today, actually, retrenchments have not picked up.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Total employment growth slowed but it did not stall.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employment growth remained robust in sectors, such as (a) Information and Communications, (b) Community, Social and Personal Services, (c) Professional Services, and (d) Financial Services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This suggests that while most employers are exercising greater caution in hiring, most are not laying off their existing workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Workers can tap on employment assistance and programmes offered by Workforce Singapore (WSG) and the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Employment and Employability Institute (e2i).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include the Career Support Programme, Career Trial and Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) that provide wage and training support to help workers access new jobs or reskill for new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Jobseekers can also consider taking up the Attach-and-Train PCPs which train the workers ahead of hiring demand and these are available in selected sectors with strong growth potential.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, WSG's Careers Connect and NTUC’s e2i career centres offer employment facilitation services, such as career coaching, employability workshops, job fairs and job matching.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Taskforce for Responsible Retrenchment and Employment Facilitation, which was formed in 2016, proactively reaches out to retrenched workers and provides them with timely employment support, including job matching.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The task force will also continue to engage retrenching companies on responsible retrenchment practices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One, in the event of a long and prolonged slowdown whereby jobs are lost, what are the levers that the Ministry is prepared to consider, including reducing the foreign manpower quota?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Two, what are the supports given to the vulnerable workers, especially those who are older and might find it harder to transit to another growth industry?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The approach that we take is to make a correct assessment of the situation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will have to ask: in any slowdown or a general downturn, what are the reasons that have caused the slowdown or the downturn?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Is it due to cyclical factors or is it due to structural factors or a combination of both?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is because the strategies that we then adopt to bring about a recovery will be very different under the circumstances, depending on what they are.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Specifically, Mr Desmond Choo asked about foreign worker quotas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We said in the Budget Debate during the Committee of Supply earlier this year that there was a need to bring us on a more sustainable path when it comes to the growth of foreign employment in the services sector.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the present time, the assessment that led to that set of recommendations has not changed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is still important for us to press on with restructuring.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I recognise where Mr Desmond Choo is coming from.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He is concerned that, if there are job losses, will older workers bear the brunt of it?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are equally concerned and we will watch very closely.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But in the meantime, that should not detract us from putting in place measures that will support senior employment for the medium to longer term because of the demographic transition that we can expect to observe in the next decade.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That set of recommendations has been considered by a tripartite work group, and I think it would not be too long before that set of recommendations is presented.
